DK26.4 is a medical diagnosis code representing a chronic or unspecified duodenal ulcer with bleeding. Within the Danish healthcare system, this specific code plays a critical role in tracking patient safety and treatment outcomes, particularly for individuals diagnosed with [[atrieflimren|atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation) [^src1]. 

Because patients with atrial fibrillation are often prescribed anticoagulant medications, they carry a heightened risk of bleeding complications. To monitor this risk, the national clinical quality indicators for atrial fibrillation in Denmark include a specific metric for the incidence of severe bleeding [^src3]. DK26.4 is one of the primary diagnostic codes used to identify cases of [[alvorlig-bloedning|Alvorlig blødning]] (severe bleeding) originating from the gastrointestinal tract [^src1]. 

The code is consistently referenced across multiple years of the national atrial fibrillation registry reports (AFDK), published by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) and the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute [^src2]. In these methodological frameworks, DK26.4 is grouped alongside a broad spectrum of other diagnostic codes—ranging from intracranial hemorrhages to urinary and respiratory tract bleeds—to ensure comprehensive surveillance of bleeding events among the atrial fibrillation patient population [^src1].

## Claims
